subject: 🏃 Saturday — Stability & Power (Wk 6)
html:
Tomorrow: Stability & Power at Cañada — recapturing the week's missed strength. Sonia's back, normal morning slot. The solo-parenting week wiped both gym sessions (Wed heavy + Fri stability); this recaptures the PT glute med / hip ER / core work that's your knee insurance. It also doubles as glute activation for Sunday's 14-miler with 5 @ MP. Keep it crisp — you're priming, not training. If you'd rather not lift the day before a long run, the fallback is a 4 mi easy shakeout at 9:30+.

Dynamic warm-up (5 min): foam roll quads/IT band 1 min each · 90/90 PAILs 30 sec each · banded lateral walks 10 each direction · Spanish squat hold 30 sec · Copenhagen plank 20 sec each side.

PT block first (non-negotiable — last full stability session was May 22, three weeks ago):

  • Side plank w/ hip abduction (top toe pointing to floor): 8 reps each side
  • Dead bug w/ banded pulldown: 2–3 × 10 slow marches
  • Chin tuck + lifts (front + diagonal): 2 reps each direction, 3-sec hold

Main work (3 × 8–10 per side, or timed):

ExerciseLoadDose
Bulgarian split squat25 lb/hand3 × 8–10 each side, 3-sec eccentric
Single-leg RDL (DB contralateral)25 lb single3 × 8–10 each side, 3-sec eccentric
Spanish squat holdLight band3 × 30–45 sec
Copenhagen plankBodyweight3 × 30 sec each side

Focus cue: Every rep crisp with a controlled 3-sec eccentric on the Bulgarians and SL-RDLs — feel the glute med engage, don't chase failure. The goal is to wake the stabilizers for tomorrow, not dig a recovery hole the day before your longest run in three weeks.

Where you are: Week 6 of 12, Phase 2 — Strength & Threshold. 6 weeks to race day, 8 days to the Presidio HM pivot test. The solo-parenting week scrambled the schedule, but the knee stayed 1/5 across every session, and yesterday's hilly run (5.5 mi, avg HR 150, +705 ft) showed the legs bounced back fully from the Jun 9 fatigue flag. Lay out the gym bag tonight and get to bed by 10 — Sunday's 14-miler is the week's marquee session.
